rules.name: Ban Throat Clearing
rules.description: Disallow conversational throat-clearing, pre-announcements, and sycophantic greetings at the beginning of prose paragraphs.
rules.rationale: Technical documentation should communicate essential information directly without introductory conversational fluff.
patterns: ^(Certainly|Sure thing|Sure|Here is|In this section|Let's dive|Note that|Allow me to|Of course)\b[!,.:]?
rules.passExample: To configure the client, supply your API key in the environment.
rules.failExample: Certainly! In this section, we will delve into configuring the client.

rules.name: Ban Filler Adverbs and Slop Words
rules.description: Flag empty buzzwords, filler adverbs, and hyperbolic adjectives that dilute technical precision.
rules.rationale: Vague superlatives weaken the authority and density of engineering prose.
rules.passExample: This update reduces memory overhead by 40%.
rules.failExample: This game-changing update seamlessly and essentially eliminates overhead.

rules.name: Avoid First-Person Plural
rules.description: Flag first-person plural pronouns ('we', 'us', 'our', 'let\'s') in technical instructions.
rules.rationale: Technical docs should focus on the reader and the system, avoiding ambiguous institutional 'we'.
patterns: \b(we recommend|we suggest|we will|in our opinion|let's|our recommendation)\b
rules.passExample: Install dependencies before starting the service.
rules.failExample: We recommend that you install dependencies first.

rules.name: Use Second Person or Imperative Mood
rules.description: Encourage direct second-person address ('you') or direct imperative mood; flag third-person passive abstraction ('the developer must...').
rules.rationale: Direct instructions are clearer and more actionable than abstract descriptions of what an anonymous persona should do.
patterns: \b(the user should|the developer should|the engineer must|the reader should)\b
rules.passExample: You can configure the timeout in config.json.
rules.failExample: The developer should configure the timeout in config.json.

rules.name: Use Active Voice
rules.description: Flag passive voice constructs (auxiliary verb + past participle + optional 'by' agent) in technical instructions.
rules.rationale: Active voice makes the actor clear and sentences more concise.
rules.passExample: The scheduler triggers the backup job nightly.
rules.failExample: The backup job is triggered nightly by the scheduler.

rules.name: High Assertion Density and Metric Grounding
rules.description: Flag qualitative performance assertions lacking concrete quantitative metrics or specific technical mechanisms.
rules.rationale: Unbacked assertions like 'vastly superior' or 'incredible speed' lack engineering utility without concrete measurements.
patterns: \b(vastly superior|incredible speed|ultra fast|blazing fast|extremely powerful|game changing performance)\b
rules.passExample: This refactoring reduces query latency from 120ms to 18ms by caching query plans.
rules.failExample: This refactoring provides vastly superior performance and incredible speed.

rules.name: State Condition Before Action
rules.description: State prerequisites or conditions before the imperative command rather than trailing after.
rules.rationale: Putting the condition first prevents the reader from executing an action before discovering it applies only conditionally.
patterns: ^[A-Z][a-z]+\s+.*\s+(?:if you want to|in order to|if you need to)\b
rules.passExample: To reload configuration, send SIGHUP to the process.
rules.failExample: Send SIGHUP to the process if you want to reload configuration.

rules.name: Heading Sentence Case
rules.description: Enforce Sentence case for all markdown headings (h1-h6) while preserving acronyms and code identifiers.
rules.rationale: Google Developer Style mandates sentence case for all headings and section titles.

rules.name: Descriptive Link Text
rules.description: Flag generic or non-descriptive link anchor text ('here', 'click here', 'link', 'this page').
rules.rationale: Links must describe their target destination so readers understand where the link leads without surrounding context.

rules.name: Serial Oxford Comma
rules.description: Encourage using the serial Oxford comma before the coordinating conjunction in lists of three or more items.
rules.rationale: Oxford commas prevent ambiguity in enumerations.
rules.passExample: Supports JSON, YAML, and TOML formats.
rules.failExample: Supports JSON, YAML and TOML formats.

rules.name: Ordered vs Unordered Sequences
rules.description: Advises using bulleted lists instead of numbered lists when list items are static descriptive points rather than chronological steps.
rules.rationale: Numbered lists imply mandatory sequential order; unordered bullet lists represent parallel properties or options.
rules.passExample: 1. Clone the repository.\n2. Install dependencies.\n3. Run the test suite.
rules.failExample: 1. High performance.\n2. Modular design.\n3. Comprehensive documentation.
